analysis.description: The paper introduces Active Domain Randomization (ADR), a novel algorithm that aims to improve agent generalization in domain transfer tasks by optimizing the sampling strategy of environment parameters. Through empirical experiments, it demonstrates that ADR can enhance the robustness and consistency of policies compared to traditional Uniform Domain Randomization (UDR), particularly in zero-shot transfer settings. ADR focuses on challenging parameter settings and leverages the discrepancies in policy rollouts to train agents more effectively.

type.justification: The paper is empirical as it presents experiments and evaluates the performance of the proposed ADR method against baseline methods in various simulated and real robotic tasks.
type.quote: In this work, we empirically examine the effects of domain randomization on agent generalization.

name.justification: The paper is centered around domain randomization and active learning techniques for reinforcement learning agents, which falls directly under the Reinforcement Learning field.
name.quote: Domain randomization is a popular technique for improving domain transfer, often used in a zero-shot setting when the target domain is unknown or cannot easily be used for training. In this work, we empirically examine the effects of domain randomization on agent generalization.

name.justification: The study addresses sim2real challenges by using domain randomization to improve transfer effectiveness from simulations to real-world environments.
name.quote: Keywords: sim2real, domain randomization, reinforcement learning
